scr_budgeting_memorizing_a_report_or_cha.purpose: Saves the settings of a budget or budget-vs-actual report — budget version, account groups, periods, properties — as a memorized report so the same package can be regenerated every month or budget cycle.
scr_budgeting_memorizing_a_report_or_cha.outcome: A reusable definition of the owner's standard budget report that produces identical layouts each time.
scr_budgeting_memorizing_a_report_or_cha.rootCause: Asset managers compare this year's budget package with last year's and each month's BVA with the prior month's. Rebuilding report settings by hand each time introduces differences (a missing group, a different version) that look like real changes.
scr_budgeting_memorizing_a_report_or_cha.ifSkipped: Budget packages differ in layout and content between cycles, and reviewers waste time on differences caused by report settings rather than performance.
redFlags: Memorized reports hard-coded to a prior budget version

scr_budgeting_memorized_reports_list.purpose: Lists memorized budget reports and charts available to the user or shared with the team, with actions to run, edit, schedule or delete them.
scr_budgeting_memorized_reports_list.outcome: A shared library of standard budget and BVA report definitions for the team.
scr_budgeting_memorized_reports_list.rootCause: When every preparer runs budget reports from the same shared definitions, owner packages look the same across properties. Personal, ad hoc definitions produce inconsistent packages that asset managers notice.
scr_budgeting_memorized_reports_list.ifSkipped: Different preparers run different definitions and owner packages vary between properties.

scr_budgeting_editing_a_memorized_report.purpose: Changes a memorized budget report's saved settings — most often switching it to the new fiscal year's approved budget version when the budget cycle rolls over.
scr_budgeting_editing_a_memorized_report.outcome: Standard budget reports point to the current approved budget.
scr_budgeting_editing_a_memorized_report.rootCause: Memorized reports keep whatever budget version they were saved with. If nobody updates them at the new year, January BVA packages compare actuals to last year's budget.
scr_budgeting_editing_a_memorized_report.ifSkipped: BVA packages compare the new year's actuals to the wrong budget, producing meaningless variances.
redFlags: January BVA run against prior-year budget

scr_budgeting_running_a_memorized_report.purpose: Runs a memorized budget report or chart with its saved settings, changing only the period — the routine way to produce monthly BVA packages.
scr_budgeting_running_a_memorized_report.outcome: Monthly budget reports produced quickly and consistently.
scr_budgeting_running_a_memorized_report.rootCause: Monthly BVA is recurring close work for every property; running from a memorized definition keeps it fast and consistent across dozens of properties.
scr_budgeting_running_a_memorized_report.ifSkipped: BVA reports are rebuilt manually every month, slowing the close and introducing inconsistencies.

scr_budgeting_scheduling_a_memorized_rep.purpose: Schedules a memorized budget report to run automatically — for example a monthly BVA delivered to regional managers after close.
scr_budgeting_scheduling_a_memorized_rep.outcome: Budget reports delivered on schedule without manual runs.
scr_budgeting_scheduling_a_memorized_rep.rootCause: Regional and asset managers want BVA as soon as the close is final; scheduling removes dependence on someone remembering across time zones.
scr_budgeting_scheduling_a_memorized_rep.ifSkipped: BVA delivery depends on manual runs and arrives late or inconsistently.
redFlags: Schedules running before the period is closed

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_memorized_repor.purpose: Deletes a memorized budget report or chart that is obsolete, duplicated or tied to a discontinued owner format.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_memorized_repor.outcome: The memorized library contains only current definitions.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_memorized_repor.rootCause: Obsolete definitions remain selectable and new staff pick them by mistake, producing budget packages in a format the owner no longer uses.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_memorized_repor.ifSkipped: Outdated definitions are used and owners receive packages in superseded formats.

scr_budgeting_edit_memorized_report_page.purpose: The page used to change a memorized budget report's name, parameters, sharing and default output format.
scr_budgeting_edit_memorized_report_page.outcome: Memorized report definitions maintained in one controlled place.
scr_budgeting_edit_memorized_report_page.rootCause: Shared definitions are used by the whole team; edits on this page change every package built from them, so they need to be deliberate and communicated.
scr_budgeting_edit_memorized_report_page.ifSkipped: Definitions change silently and packages shift without anyone knowing why.
redFlags: Shared reports edited without notifying the team

scr_budgeting_schedule_memorized_report_.purpose: The page where the frequency, time, recipients and output format of a scheduled memorized budget report are set.
scr_budgeting_schedule_memorized_report_.outcome: Automated distribution of budget reports to the right people.
scr_budgeting_schedule_memorized_report_.rootCause: Recipients and timing determine whether scheduled BVA is useful; sending before close finishes distributes preliminary numbers as if final.
scr_budgeting_schedule_memorized_report_.ifSkipped: Preliminary BVA reaches owners, or reports go to people who have left.

scr_budgeting_working_budget_report.purpose: Reports a working budget's amounts by account and period, optionally compared to actuals or another budget, for review before publishing.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_report.outcome: A printable or exportable view of a draft budget for review meetings.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_report.rootCause: Budget review meetings with regional and asset managers need a clean report of the draft, not a system screen; this report provides it directly from the working budget.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_report.ifSkipped: Drafts are reviewed from ad hoc exports that may not match the system version.
redFlags: Report run on the wrong working budget

scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.purpose: Selects the working budget, properties, accounts, periods and comparison columns and runs the Working Budget report.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.outcome: A review report scoped to exactly what the meeting will discuss.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.rootCause: Review meetings focus on specific properties and account groups; well-chosen parameters produce a short, relevant report instead of a data dump.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.ifSkipped: Review reports are too broad and important lines are lost in them.

scr_budgeting_using_the_select_multiple_.purpose: Selects several GL accounts at once for the Working Budget report — for example all utility accounts or all payroll-related accounts.
scr_budgeting_using_the_select_multiple_.outcome: Focused reports on a chosen set of accounts.
scr_budgeting_using_the_select_multiple_.rootCause: Reviewers often focus on a category spread across several accounts; selecting them together avoids running multiple reports.
scr_budgeting_using_the_select_multiple_.ifSkipped: Category reviews require several separate reports and are slower.

scr_budgeting_working_budget_report_colu.purpose: Explains the Working Budget report columns — account, periods, totals, comparison budget or actuals, and variance.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_report_colu.outcome: Reviewers read draft budgets and their comparisons correctly.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_report_colu.rootCause: Misreading which column is the draft and which is the comparison leads to discussions about the wrong numbers in review meetings.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_report_colu.ifSkipped: Review decisions are based on misread columns.
redFlags: Column headers not labeled with version names

scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.purpose: Runs the Account Groups Hierarchy report from the Reports area of Forecasting & Planning to check how accounts roll up into groups used in budgets and BVA reports.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.outcome: Budget reporting structures verified before the budget cycle.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.rootCause: Budget reports use account groups; if a group is missing accounts, the budget package understates totals. Checking the hierarchy before budget season prevents that.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_r.ifSkipped: Budget packages have incomplete subtotals that are only discovered during owner review.
redFlags: Hierarchy totals not tying to trial balance

scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.purpose: Chooses the groups, period and locations and runs the Account Groups Hierarchy report from the budgeting Reports area.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.outcome: A focused hierarchy check for the groups used in budgeting.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.rootCause: Checking only the groups used by the budget package keeps the review manageable and targeted before budget season.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.ifSkipped: Hierarchy reviews are skipped because the full report is too large.
redFlags: Report run for a period with no activity

scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_c.purpose: Explains the columns of the hierarchy report when run from budgeting — group, level, members and values.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_c.outcome: Correct interpretation of how budget subtotals are built.
scr_budgeting_account_groups_hierarchy_c.rootCause: Understanding levels and members lets the accountant confirm that NOI and category subtotals in budget reports contain exactly the intended accounts.
redFlags: Accounts appearing in two sibling groups

scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_report.purpose: Lists the chart of accounts — numbers, names, types, normal balances and statuses — used to confirm the account structure before building budgets.
scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_report.outcome: A verified chart of accounts for budgeting.
scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_report.rootCause: Budgets built on inactive or wrongly typed accounts never match actuals; reviewing the chart first prevents that.
scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_report.ifSkipped: Budget lines are built on accounts that will never receive actuals.
redFlags: Active accounts with no activity for years

scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.purpose: Sets filters (account ranges, types, status) and runs the Chart of Accounts report.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.outcome: A chart listing for the account ranges relevant to the review.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.rootCause: Reviewing the operating expense range separately from balance sheet ranges keeps budget-structure reviews focused.
scr_budgeting_customizing_and_running_th.ifSkipped: Chart reviews are too broad to be useful.
redFlags: Inactive accounts included in budget ranges

scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_columns.purpose: Explains the Chart of Accounts report columns — number, name, type, normal balance, category and status.
scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_columns.rootCause: Type and normal balance columns reveal misconfigured accounts that would display with wrong signs in budget and financial reports.
scr_budgeting_chart_of_accounts_columns.ifSkipped: Misconfigured accounts produce wrong signs in reports.
redFlags: Revenue accounts with debit normal balance

scr_budgeting_setting_up_forecasting_and.purpose: Chapter on setting up Forecasting & Planning — subscription, permissions, dimensions and segments — before budgeting begins.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_forecasting_and.outcome: A configured planning application aligned with the company's structure.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_forecasting_and.rootCause: Budgets depend on dimensions (locations, departments) and permissions being correct; setup mistakes surface only when budgets are built, under deadline.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_forecasting_and.ifSkipped: Budget season starts with missing dimensions or access, delaying the budget.
redFlags: Setup started after budget season began

scr_budgeting_setting_up_the_forecasting.purpose: Explains the application-level settings of Forecasting & Planning — how working budgets are seeded, which GL budget they publish to and how actuals are advanced — configured once before the first budget cycle.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_the_forecasting.outcome: The application is ready for budget creation.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_the_forecasting.rootCause: Application settings determine how working budgets behave (seeding, publishing targets); they must be configured once, deliberately.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_the_forecasting.ifSkipped: Working budgets behave unexpectedly, for example publishing to the wrong GL budget.

scr_budgeting_forecasting_and_planning_s.purpose: The setup workflow: subscribe, assign permissions, set up dimensions and segments, then configure payroll and fee tables before building budgets.
scr_budgeting_forecasting_and_planning_s.outcome: Setup performed in the right order.
scr_budgeting_forecasting_and_planning_s.rootCause: Later steps depend on earlier ones (payroll needs employees and locations); following the order avoids rework.
scr_budgeting_forecasting_and_planning_s.ifSkipped: Setup steps fail because prerequisites are missing, and budget season starts with the application half-configured.

scr_budgeting_subscribing_to_forecasting.purpose: Enables the Forecasting & Planning subscription under Company > Setup > Subscriptions so the application becomes available.
scr_budgeting_subscribing_to_forecasting.outcome: The planning application is available to licensed users.
scr_budgeting_subscribing_to_forecasting.rootCause: Without the subscription, working budgets, payroll planning and management fee planning are unavailable and budgeting falls back to spreadsheets.
scr_budgeting_subscribing_to_forecasting.ifSkipped: Budgeting is done in spreadsheets outside the system.

scr_budgeting_setting_up_permissions_for.purpose: Assigns permissions for Forecasting & Planning — who can create working budgets, edit them, publish them and view payroll detail.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_permissions_for.outcome: Budget editing and publishing restricted to the right roles, and payroll detail protected.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_permissions_for.rootCause: Publishing overwrites the official GL budget and payroll planning exposes individual salaries; both need restricted access.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_permissions_for.ifSkipped: Anyone can publish budgets or view salaries.
redFlags: Offshore preparers with publish rights and no reviewer

scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions_for_.purpose: Sets up the dimensions used in budgeting — vendors, customers, employees, departments and locations — so budgets can be built and analyzed at those levels.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions_for_.outcome: Budgets can be planned by location, department or other dimensions.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions_for_.rootCause: Owners often want budgets by building or department; that requires the dimensions to exist before budgeting.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions_for_.ifSkipped: Budgets cannot be built or analyzed by building, department or location, which many owners require.
redFlags: Dimensions not aligned between actuals and budgets

scr_budgeting_vendors.purpose: The Vendors dimension as used in budgeting — allowing budgets or analysis by vendor, such as contract services by vendor.
scr_budgeting_vendors.outcome: Contract-driven budget lines can be tied to specific vendors.
scr_budgeting_vendors.rootCause: Many budget lines are driven by vendor contracts (landscaping, elevator, pest control); linking to vendors makes the basis clear.
scr_budgeting_vendors.ifSkipped: Contract budgets cannot be traced to vendors.

scr_budgeting_vendors_suppliers_list.purpose: The vendors list reached from planning setup, used to confirm vendors exist before budgeting by vendor.
scr_budgeting_vendors_suppliers_list.outcome: Vendor records available for vendor-level planning.
scr_budgeting_vendors_suppliers_list.rootCause: Vendor-level budgets need vendor records; checking the list avoids creating duplicates from planning.
scr_budgeting_vendors_suppliers_list.ifSkipped: Duplicate vendors are created, which later cause A/P duplicate payment risk.
redFlags: Vendors created from planning without master data review

scr_budgeting_adding_vendor_supplier_rec.purpose: Adds a vendor record from the planning setup area, for example a new contractor included in next year's budget.
scr_budgeting_adding_vendor_supplier_rec.outcome: The vendor exists for planning and later for A/P.
scr_budgeting_adding_vendor_supplier_rec.rootCause: New contracts planned for the budget year may involve new vendors; adding them must still follow vendor master controls (W-9, verification).
scr_budgeting_adding_vendor_supplier_rec.ifSkipped: Vendors are created without verification, bypassing A/P vendor controls.

scr_budgeting_editing_vendor_records.purpose: Edits a vendor record from the Forecasting & Planning setup area — for example updating contract terms that drive a contract-services budget line — subject to the same vendor master controls as A/P.
scr_budgeting_editing_vendor_records.outcome: Vendor details stay current for both planning and payment.
scr_budgeting_editing_vendor_records.rootCause: Vendor edits affect payments and 1099s; even when made from planning they must follow vendor change controls.
scr_budgeting_editing_vendor_records.ifSkipped: Vendor changes made from planning bypass A/P change controls, including bank-detail verification.
redFlags: Bank detail changes made from planning screens

scr_budgeting_viewing_vendor_supplier_re.purpose: Views vendor records from planning to confirm vendor details used in budget assumptions.
scr_budgeting_viewing_vendor_supplier_re.outcome: Budget assumptions tied to correct vendor information.
scr_budgeting_viewing_vendor_supplier_re.rootCause: Checking vendor records confirms the right contractor is associated with contract-based budget lines.
scr_budgeting_viewing_vendor_supplier_re.ifSkipped: Budget lines reference the wrong vendor.

scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.purpose: Deletes or inactivates a vendor from the planning setup area — inactivating vendors with payment history, and deleting only records created in error.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.outcome: Inactive vendors are no longer used in plans or payments.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.rootCause: Vendors with payment history must be inactivated rather than deleted to preserve A/P and 1099 history.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.ifSkipped: Obsolete vendors remain usable or history is lost.

scr_budgeting_vendor_supplier_informatio.purpose: The vendor record page reached from planning setup, showing contact, payment terms and contract details that planners use to budget contract services such as landscaping or elevator maintenance.
scr_budgeting_vendor_supplier_informatio.outcome: Full vendor detail available during planning.
scr_budgeting_vendor_supplier_informatio.rootCause: Planners need vendor details (contract terms, payment terms) to budget contract services accurately.
scr_budgeting_vendor_supplier_informatio.ifSkipped: Contract budgets built without contract detail.

scr_budgeting_customers.purpose: The Customers dimension as used in budgeting — for commercial tenants, affiliates or ancillary contract partners whose revenue is budgeted by customer.
scr_budgeting_customers.outcome: Revenue from specific customers (e.g., a laundry contractor or cell tower) budgeted and tracked individually.
scr_budgeting_customers.rootCause: Ancillary revenue contracts have specific terms and escalations; budgeting them by customer ties the budget to the contract.
scr_budgeting_customers.ifSkipped: Contract revenue is budgeted as a lump and escalations are missed.

scr_budgeting_customers_list.purpose: The customers list reached from planning setup to confirm customers exist for customer-level budgets.
scr_budgeting_customers_list.outcome: Customer records available for revenue planning.
scr_budgeting_customers_list.rootCause: Customer-level revenue budgets require customer records; checking prevents duplicates.

scr_budgeting_adding_customers.purpose: Adds a customer record from planning, for example a new ancillary services partner included in next year's revenue budget.
scr_budgeting_adding_customers.outcome: New revenue partners exist for planning and billing.
scr_budgeting_adding_customers.rootCause: New contracts planned for the year need customer records before revenue can be budgeted and later billed.
scr_budgeting_adding_customers.ifSkipped: Planned revenue cannot be tied to a customer.

scr_budgeting_viewing_or_editing_a_custo.purpose: Views or edits a customer record from planning setup — for example updating a laundry or cell-tower contract's escalation terms that drive next year's ancillary revenue budget.
scr_budgeting_viewing_or_editing_a_custo.outcome: Customer details kept current for planning and billing.
scr_budgeting_viewing_or_editing_a_custo.rootCause: Contract changes (renewals, rate changes) must be reflected on the customer record to budget and bill correctly.
scr_budgeting_viewing_or_editing_a_custo.ifSkipped: Revenue budgets and billing continue on outdated contract terms.

scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.purpose: Deletes or inactivates a customer record from planning setup when a contract ends, inactivating customers with A/R history rather than deleting them.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.outcome: Only active customers used in planning.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.rootCause: Customers with invoices and payments must be inactivated so A/R history, aging and audit trails remain intact; deleting them would orphan their transaction history.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.ifSkipped: Obsolete customers budgeted or A/R history lost.

scr_budgeting_customer_information_page.purpose: The customer record page reached from planning, with contact, terms and document settings.
scr_budgeting_customer_information_page.outcome: Full customer detail available for revenue planning.
scr_budgeting_customer_information_page.rootCause: Revenue planning for contract customers depends on accurate terms stored on the customer record.
scr_budgeting_customer_information_page.ifSkipped: Revenue budgets built without contract terms.

scr_budgeting_employees.purpose: The Employees dimension used to create and edit employee records so payroll can be planned and reported by employee.
scr_budgeting_employees.outcome: Employee records available for payroll planning and allocation.
scr_budgeting_employees.rootCause: Payroll planning needs an employee dimension to budget and allocate each person's cost to properties.
scr_budgeting_employees.ifSkipped: Payroll cannot be planned or allocated by employee, so payroll budgets are rough totals.

scr_budgeting_importing_employees.purpose: Imports employee records in bulk from a template, typically from the HR or payroll system at budget season.
scr_budgeting_importing_employees.outcome: An up-to-date employee roster loaded for payroll planning.
scr_budgeting_importing_employees.rootCause: Rosters change constantly; importing from HR is the only practical way to start the payroll budget from current staff.
scr_budgeting_importing_employees.ifSkipped: Payroll budgets start from outdated rosters.
redFlags: Import not reconciled to HR headcount

scr_budgeting_employees_list_2.purpose: The employees list within Forecasting & Planning dimensions setup, used to confirm which employee records exist, their positions and locations before payroll is calculated.
scr_budgeting_employees_list_2.outcome: Visibility of employee records available to planning.
scr_budgeting_employees_list_2.rootCause: Confirming the roster before payroll calculation catches missing or terminated staff.
scr_budgeting_employees_list_2.ifSkipped: Payroll is calculated on a roster that still includes departed staff or misses new hires.

scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee.purpose: Adds an employee in dimensions setup — for planned hires or when HR import is not used.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee.outcome: Planned staff available for payroll budgets.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee.rootCause: Planned hires and open positions must exist as employee records before the payroll model can budget them; otherwise the payroll budget reflects only current staff and understates next year's cost.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee.ifSkipped: Planned hires are omitted and payroll is under-budgeted.

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_employ.purpose: Views or edits an employee's dimension record — position, home location, status and department — which determines where that person's payroll is budgeted.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_employ.rootCause: Location and status drive where payroll is budgeted; errors send payroll to the wrong property.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_employ.ifSkipped: Payroll is budgeted at the wrong property or department.

scr_budgeting_deleting_employees.purpose: Deletes employee dimension records created in error, such as duplicates from a manual entry and a later HR import of the same person.
scr_budgeting_deleting_employees.rootCause: Duplicate employee records double-count that person's wages, taxes and benefits in the payroll budget, overstating payroll for the property.
scr_budgeting_deleting_employees.ifSkipped: Payroll is overstated by duplicate employees and the property budget looks unaffordable.

scr_budgeting_employee_information_page.purpose: The employee record page in dimensions setup holding position, location, department and status — the attributes the payroll model uses to calculate and place each person's cost.
scr_budgeting_employee_information_page.rootCause: Employee attributes drive payroll calculation and allocation; completeness matters.
scr_budgeting_employee_information_page.ifSkipped: Payroll calculations miss attributes and place costs at the wrong property or department.
